author: DYLAN LOVAN - Associated Press
title: Colonel Sanders' Personal Items Up for Auction
text:
• KFC founder Colonel Sanders' pressure cooker, black bow tie, and dozens of other personal items are up for public auction.
• The auction includes his former home and the Claudia Sanders Dinner House.
• Harland Sanders established the Shelbyville property as the first headquarters of his restaurant business in the late 1950s.
• He sold the property in 1974 to Tommy and Cherry Settle, who have run the restaurant since then.
• Online pre-bidding concludes with a live, in-person auction for the Sanders memorabilia on Tuesday evening.
• Sealed bids for the restaurant and Sanders' former 5,000-square-foot home, which he named Blackwood Hall, will be taken until Friday.
• Sanders' personal watches, an original cash register, his cutlery set, a bust sculpted by his daughter, and a commercial gas range from the colonel's former residence are among the items up for bidding.
• Sanders sold KFC in 1964 to a group of investors, but continued as a brand ambassador for the company.
• Menish called Sanders a “marketing genius” for creating the character of the colonel.
• A personal 1964 planner with a handwritten herbs and spices recipe is up for auction.
• The planner was the subject of an early 2000s lawsuit filed by the KFC Corp. to keep the contents private.
• KFC later dropped the legal action, saying after reviewing the planner the ingredients didn’t match Sanders' secret blend of 11 herbs and spices, and it was likely a recipe for stuffing.
• One of Sanders' signature black bow ties is up for auction, with the highest online bid being more than $2,000 on Monday.
• Auctioneer Jonathan Klunk said that Colonel Sanders wore clip-ons with his signature black bow tie.
summary: Harland Sanders, still known as the face of the worldwide chain originally known as Kentucky Fried Chicken, established the Shelbyville property as the first headquarters of his restaurant business in the late 1950s. He sold the property, which included his home and the Claudia Sanders Dinner House, in 1974 to Tommy and Cherry Settle, who have run the restaurant since then. Sanders’ personal watches, an original cash register, his cutlery set, a bust sculpted by his daughter and a commercial gas range from the colonel's former residence are among the items up for bidding.
